zoningRules.text: Permitted uses in the R-2 zone. Household living, group living, and accessory uses are allowed. Retail sales and service, office and industrial uses are prohibited except home occupations.

Maximum height. The maximum height of structures in the R-2 zone is 30 feet, measured from the base point to the highest point of the roof, excluding parapets up to 4 feet and mechanical equipment that is set back at least 15 feet from all roof edges.
Maximum floor area ratio. The floor area ratio (FAR) in the R-2 zone is 0.5 to 1. Floor area within structured parking that is below grade is not counted toward FAR.
Maximum building coverage. Building coverage in the R-2 zone may not exceed 40 percent of the site area. Eaves, awnings and uncovered decks less than 30 inches above grade are excluded.
Setbacks. The minimum front setback is 20 feet, the minimum side setback is 5 feet, and the minimum rear setback is 15 feet. On a corner lot both street-facing sides are treated as front lot lines.

Minimum required parking. Household living requires 1.5 off-street spaces per dwelling unit. Sites within 500 feet of a frequent-service transit stop may reduce the minimum by 50 percent (see 33.266.110.C).
Required outdoor area. Multi-dwelling development must provide 36 square feet of outdoor area per dwelling unit, which may be provided on roof decks or in courtyards.

Design standards. Street-facing facades must include windows on at least 15 percent of the ground-floor wall area, and ground-floor dwelling units must have their finished floor at least 2 feet above the adjacent sidewalk grade unless the ground floor is in non-residential use.
Permitted uses in the R-5 zone. Household living, group living, and accessory uses are allowed. Retail sales and service, office and industrial uses are prohibited except home occupations.

Maximum height. The maximum height of structures in the R-5 zone is 45 feet, measured from the base point to the highest point of the roof, excluding parapets up to 4 feet and mechanical equipment that is set back at least 15 feet from all roof edges.
Maximum floor area ratio. The floor area ratio (FAR) in the R-5 zone is 1.5 to 1. Floor area within structured parking that is below grade is not counted toward FAR.
Maximum building coverage. Building coverage in the R-5 zone may not exceed 50 percent of the site area. Eaves, awnings and uncovered decks less than 30 inches above grade are excluded.
Setbacks. The minimum front setback is 10 feet, the minimum side setback is 5 feet, and the minimum rear setback is 10 feet. On a corner lot both street-facing sides are treated as front lot lines.

Minimum required parking. Household living requires 1 off-street spaces per dwelling unit. Sites within 500 feet of a frequent-service transit stop may reduce the minimum by 50 percent (see 33.266.110.C).
Required outdoor area. Multi-dwelling development must provide 36 square feet of outdoor area per dwelling unit, which may be provided on roof decks or in courtyards.

Design standards. Street-facing facades must include windows on at least 15 percent of the ground-floor wall area, and ground-floor dwelling units must have their finished floor at least 2 feet above the adjacent sidewalk grade unless the ground floor is in non-residential use.
Permitted uses in the RM-3 zone. Household living, group living, and accessory uses are allowed. Retail sales and service, office and industrial uses are prohibited except home occupations.

Maximum height. The maximum height of structures in the RM-3 zone is 65 feet, measured from the base point to the highest point of the roof, excluding parapets up to 4 feet and mechanical equipment that is set back at least 15 feet from all roof edges.
Maximum floor area ratio. The floor area ratio (FAR) in the RM-3 zone is 2.5 to 1. Floor area within structured parking that is below grade is not counted toward FAR.
Maximum building coverage. Building coverage in the RM-3 zone may not exceed 60 percent of the site area. Eaves, awnings and uncovered decks less than 30 inches above grade are excluded.
Setbacks. The minimum front setback is 10 feet, the minimum side setback is 5 feet, and the minimum rear setback is 10 feet. On a corner lot both street-facing sides are treated as front lot lines.

Minimum required parking. Household living requires 0.75 off-street spaces per dwelling unit. Sites within 500 feet of a frequent-service transit stop may reduce the minimum by 50 percent (see 33.266.110.C).
Required outdoor area. Multi-dwelling development must provide 36 square feet of outdoor area per dwelling unit, which may be provided on roof decks or in courtyards.

Design standards. Street-facing facades must include windows on at least 15 percent of the ground-floor wall area, and ground-floor dwelling units must have their finished floor at least 2 feet above the adjacent sidewalk grade unless the ground floor is in non-residential use.

Height bonus. Sites that provide at least 10 percent of dwelling units as affordable to households earning no more than 60 percent of the area median income, for a period of 99 years, may increase the maximum height by 15 feet where the site is within the Transit Overlay shown on Map 510-3. The bonus does not apply to sites within the Waterfront Overlay.

Permitted uses in the CM-2 zone. Household living, retail sales and service, office, commercial parking and quick vehicle servicing are allowed outright. Industrial service is allowed up to 5,000 square feet of floor area per site.

Maximum height. The maximum height of structures in the CM-2 zone is 75 feet, measured from the base point to the highest point of the roof, excluding parapets up to 4 feet and mechanical equipment that is set back at least 15 feet from all roof edges.
Maximum floor area ratio. The floor area ratio (FAR) in the CM-2 zone is 5.0 to 1. Floor area within structured parking that is below grade is not counted toward FAR.
Maximum building coverage. Building coverage in the CM-2 zone may not exceed 85 percent of the site area. Eaves, awnings and uncovered decks less than 30 inches above grade are excluded.
Setbacks. The minimum front setback is 0 feet, the minimum side setback is 0 feet, and the minimum rear setback is 10 feet. On a corner lot both street-facing sides are treated as front lot lines.

Minimum required parking. Household living requires 0.5 off-street spaces per dwelling unit. Sites within 500 feet of a frequent-service transit stop may reduce the minimum by 50 percent (see 33.266.110.C).
Required outdoor area. Multi-dwelling development must provide 36 square feet of outdoor area per dwelling unit, which may be provided on roof decks or in courtyards.

Design standards. Street-facing facades must include windows on at least 15 percent of the ground-floor wall area, and ground-floor dwelling units must have their finished floor at least 2 feet above the adjacent sidewalk grade unless the ground floor is in non-residential use.

Ground floor active uses. On sites with street frontage on an arterial street, at least 50 percent of the ground-floor street-facing wall must be in retail sales and service, office, or other active use, with a minimum ground-floor height of 15 feet floor to ceiling.

Height bonus. Sites that provide at least 10 percent of dwelling units as affordable to households earning no more than 60 percent of the area median income, for a period of 99 years, may increase the maximum height by 20 feet where the site is within the Transit Overlay shown on Map 510-3. The bonus does not apply to sites within the Waterfront Overlay.

Permitted uses in the CX-4 zone. Household living, retail sales and service, office, commercial parking and quick vehicle servicing are allowed outright. Industrial service is allowed up to 5,000 square feet of floor area per site.

Maximum height. The maximum height of structures in the CX-4 zone is 150 feet, measured from the base point to the highest point of the roof, excluding parapets up to 4 feet and mechanical equipment that is set back at least 15 feet from all roof edges.
Maximum floor area ratio. The floor area ratio (FAR) in the CX-4 zone is 6.0 to 1. Floor area within structured parking that is below grade is not counted toward FAR.
Maximum building coverage. Building coverage in the CX-4 zone may not exceed 100 percent of the site area. Eaves, awnings and uncovered decks less than 30 inches above grade are excluded.
Setbacks. The minimum front setback is 0 feet, the minimum side setback is 0 feet, and the minimum rear setback is 0 feet. On a corner lot both street-facing sides are treated as front lot lines.
Minimum required parking. There is no minimum parking requirement in the CX-4 zone. Bicycle parking is required at 1.5 spaces per dwelling unit.
Required outdoor area. Multi-dwelling development must provide 36 square feet of outdoor area per dwelling unit, which may be provided on roof decks or in courtyards.

Design standards. Street-facing facades must include windows on at least 15 percent of the ground-floor wall area, and ground-floor dwelling units must have their finished floor at least 2 feet above the adjacent sidewalk grade unless the ground floor is in non-residential use.

Ground floor active uses. On sites with street frontage on an arterial street, at least 50 percent of the ground-floor street-facing wall must be in retail sales and service, office, or other active use, with a minimum ground-floor height of 15 feet floor to ceiling.

Height bonus. Sites that provide at least 10 percent of dwelling units as affordable to households earning no more than 60 percent of the area median income, for a period of 99 years, may increase the maximum height by 50 feet where the site is within the Transit Overlay shown on Map 510-3. The bonus does not apply to sites within the Waterfront Overlay.
Permitted uses in the IG zone. Manufacturing and production, warehouse and freight movement, and industrial service are allowed; household living is prohibited.

Maximum height. The maximum height of structures in the IG zone is 55 feet, measured from the base point to the highest point of the roof, excluding parapets up to 4 feet and mechanical equipment that is set back at least 15 feet from all roof edges.
Maximum floor area ratio. The floor area ratio (FAR) in the IG zone is 2.0 to 1. Floor area within structured parking that is below grade is not counted toward FAR.
Maximum building coverage. Building coverage in the IG zone may not exceed 70 percent of the site area. Eaves, awnings and uncovered decks less than 30 inches above grade are excluded.
Setbacks. The minimum front setback is 10 feet, the minimum side setback is 10 feet, and the minimum rear setback is 10 feet. On a corner lot both street-facing sides are treated as front lot lines.

Minimum required parking. Household living requires 0.5 off-street spaces per dwelling unit. Sites within 500 feet of a frequent-service transit stop may reduce the minimum by 50 percent (see 33.266.110.C).
Required outdoor area. Multi-dwelling development must provide 36 square feet of outdoor area per dwelling unit, which may be provided on roof decks or in courtyards.

Design standards. Street-facing facades must include windows on at least 15 percent of the ground-floor wall area, and ground-floor dwelling units must have their finished floor at least 2 feet above the adjacent sidewalk grade unless the ground floor is in non-residential use.
